notes:
- Every table in the reader has a ⋯ menu above it. "Copy table" puts the
  table on the clipboard as both HTML and tab-separated text, so it pastes as
  a real table into mail, a spreadsheet or a document and as plain text into
  a chat window. The HTML carries structure and a grey border and no colour,
  background or font, so it takes the destination's theme instead of dragging
  dark-mode white text onto a white page. The menu also copies the table as
  markdown or CSV and opens the Table view, which until now only a table too
  wide for the pane offered. The Table view's own export gains the same
  "Copy table" for the sorted, filtered view.
- A folder can be ignored from the reader. The document actions menu now
  says "Ignore doc" for the per-file rule and adds "Ignore directory", which
  opens a picker over the document's own folder chain: project first, the
  file's folder last, each level with the number of indexed documents it
  holds and the list for the one picked. Confirming writes one `dir/**` rule,
  the same one the triage tray and the workspace tree write, and Settings ›
  Corpus removes it again.
- Settings has a Mobile sync section for the sitrep-sync mirror. It shows
  whether this Mac has a sync account, turns the pusher's watch on and off
  (the app's server runs it as a child and resumes it at boot), shows the
  pairing QR code behind an explicit click with a note on what the code
  grants, reports how many documents were pushed and when a phone last
  pulled, and can stop and wipe the mirror behind a confirm. It needs a
  sitrep-sync checkout and your own worker; without them the section says so
  and names the command that sets one up.
- With no window open, sitrep's background git sweep runs hourly instead of
  every 5 minutes. Opening a window resumes the 5-minute pace, and a sweep
  that is overdue runs right then. Commits still show up while nobody is
  looking: a repo's own .git events drive its refresh at any pace, so the
  stretch only delays the catch-up for changes macOS never reported.

- sitrep stays out of macOS's "Using Significant Energy" list. The background
  git refresh reran every repo's full commit history every five minutes, which
  kept a git process alive 65% of the time and the server near 11% CPU around
  the clock. It now rereads history only when a repo's HEAD actually moved;
  branch, ahead/behind and the clean/modified state of documents still refresh
  every sweep.

- A document with no row in the list beside it says why in the reader's own
  header: an accent strip under the breadcrumb reads "This document is in
  another workspace / project" and offers "Switch to <name>", naming the
  workspace or project the click moves the list to. A document the view or
  filters hide reads "The active view or filters hide this document" with
  "Reset view and filters", the search, refinements and view preset that
  click clears. The filters case is new: the list can say it is hiding the
  document you are reading, and the answer comes from the list's own query
  rather than a guess. Replaces 0.7.0's muted row under the list header,
  which read as part of the header.
- A `doc.md:311` open shows the line-number gutter for that visit, with the
  Settings preference untouched: the number asked for is readable on
  arrival, and moving to another document puts the gutter back the way the
  preference says. Reopening the same file plainly no longer replays the
  old line landing either.
- "Check for Updates…" shows its work: the menu item opens Settings › About,
  which checks on open - a spinner while the manifest is read, then "You're
  on X, the latest" or the offer. With background download off the offer is
  one "Download and install" button; that click is also the restart consent,
  so the app relaunches as the new version the moment the download lands.
  An update already downloaded keeps the shortcut: the menu item, titled
  "Restart to update to X", installs directly.
- The menu works with the last window closed. Closing it keeps sitrep and
  its menu bar alive, the Mac convention, but "Settings…" and "Check for
  Updates…" were dead clicks there in every build through 0.7.0: the shell
  answers a menu click by dispatching into the page, and there was no page.
  The click now rebuilds the window and carries the action into it.

- A phase whose heading carries no state word now reads its own checklist:
  every box under the heading ticked is done, some ticked is in flight. The
  phase chip's receipt names the tally and jumps to the first box. A heading
  word, a tracking bullet or the status line still outranks the ticks.
- A phase can be superseded: from its own heading word (`SUPERSEDED`,
  `OBSOLETE`, `REJECTED` and the rest of that list) or inherited from a
  superseded document, which retires every phase it never finished. The
  phase strip draws a retired phase as a red-hatched segment, the count
  beside the strip disappears once nothing is open (every phase done or
  struck: the segments already say it), and a retired plan no longer
  counts as in
  flight, planned or claiming work for the staleness badges. `sitrep_doc`
  and the list rows carry `phases_open` beside `phases_done`.
- A document opened from outside the list's scope (a followed link, Cmd+O,
  a Finder open) names the mismatch: a one-line row under the list header
  reads "Reading in workspace / project", and clicking either takes the
  list there while the reader stays open. The list never switches on its
  own.
- The reader's breadcrumb carries a copy button for the document's full
  path.

- The document list gives every fact a fixed home: a status icon then the
  title on the first line (dashed circle = no status recorded, half-filled =
  in progress, check = shipped), signal chips and the phase strip on the
  second, time, commits and git state bottom left, the project tag bottom
  right. Rich rows dropped from five lines to three, titles align down the
  whole list, and the status excerpt no longer repeats what the badge says.
- Dragging the list/reader divider resizes both panes live: the document
  re-wraps as the pointer moves, and the expensive table re-fit waits for
  the release instead of running every frame.
- Settings save themselves: changes land once you pause, the header says so,
  and Save/Cancel are gone. Creating a workspace stays a deliberate click -
  the folder step's own "Create workspace" button - and removing one asks
  "Really remove?" first.
- Adding a workspace indexes only that workspace instead of re-reading every
  other one; renaming a workspace, changing its monogram or adjusting
  staleness thresholds reindexes nothing at all.
- Picking a folder and saving no longer answers `workspace id "" must be
  lowercase letters, digits and dashes` - the create action commits the
  picked folder itself.
- Cold opens survive launch: a document double-clicked in Finder while the
  app is still starting lands in the reader once the server is up, and
  previews refresh and link from disk.

- Settings › About can make sitrep your default Markdown app: one click and
  double-clicking .md, .markdown and .mdown files in Finder opens them here.
  Per-user, no admin prompt, undoable anytime via Finder's Get Info › Open
  With - and the choice survives updates, since macOS keys it on the app's
  identity rather than its version.
- Installing got the standard Mac treatment: the download opens as a window
  where you drag sitrep into Applications, with the layout and background
  to match.
- The 14-day trial clock now heals itself: deleting individual files in
  sitrep's app data no longer restarts the trial.

- sitrep now has a license: a 14-day full trial starts on first launch of
  the packaged app, a key entered in Settings › License (or on the gate
  screen after the trial) is verified offline - no account, no activation
  server - and a licensed app never phones home about it.
- First launch no longer trips the "Apple Music, your music and video
  activity, and your media library" permission prompt: the folder walk
  behind the getting-started page skips ~/Music, ~/Movies and ~/Pictures
  until you deliberately browse into one.
- The Desktop/Documents/Downloads permission prompts on first launch now
  say why sitrep is asking (it counts markdown so you can choose what to
  index) instead of appearing as bare system dialogs.

- The app updates itself: it checks sitrep.md shortly after launch and
  daily, downloads a new version in the background (a setting turns that
  off), and installs only when you click "Restart to update" or on your way
  out of a quit - never behind your back. Downgrades are refused. (The
  0.3.0-beta.1 updater line, promoted to stable after a beta-to-stable
  round-trip on a real install.)
- Settings gains an About section: version, the update channel
  (stable/beta), the update's state and notes, and the third-party licenses
  of everything that ships in the app.
- "Check for Updates…" in the sitrep menu answers honestly: "You're on
  X, the latest", or the offer - and becomes "Restart to update to X" once
  a new version is downloaded.

- sitrep runs as a self-contained Mac app: the server ships inside
  sitrep.app as a compiled sidecar, so it needs no runtime, no checkout and
  no setup on the machine it lands on.
- Double-clicking a markdown file (or "Open with sitrep") lands in the
  running app on that file, and on the exact line when a terminal hands one
  over.
- The app is signed and notarized: Gatekeeper opens it first try, offline,
  with no right-click ceremony.
- The app owns the server's lifecycle: it starts it on a free port,
  restarts it if it dies, and leaves nothing running on either quit path.
